title: Biological Approach Adventure 2: Neurotransmitters & Hormones
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet dopamine, serotonin, cortisol and oxytocin.
meta_desc: IBDP Psychology Biological: neurotransmitters dopamine and serotonin, hormones cortisol and oxytocin.
final_note: You linked four key biochemicals to mood, stress and bonding.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Neurotransmitters bridge the synaptic gap.

Dopamine — reward and motor control. Excess in mesolimbic pathway linked to schizophrenia (dopamine hypothesis). Low in Parkinson's disease.

Serotonin — mood and sleep. SSRIs raise its synaptic level in depression (Kirsch et al., 2008, debate the effect size).

The HPA axis fires under stress.

Hypothalamus → pituitary → adrenal cortex → cortisol.

Chronic cortisol harms hippocampal neurons, impairing memory (Newcomer et al., 1999).

Oxytocin from the posterior pituitary supports labour, breastfeeding, social bonding and trust.

Kosfeld et al. (2005): intranasal oxytocin raised trust in an investment game.

Newer studies (Nave et al., 2015) show mixed results — replication crisis warning.
